context_only_not_derivation_inputs.reason: The Interaction family's semantic intents (a grab started, a select performed) are the seam this family binds haptic events to through a binding table; the interaction routing model itself is not re-derived here and contributes no evidence for haptic identity, kind, or profile semantics

The Audio family's event identity is the second seam this family binds to, so one source intent can fire an audio event and a haptic event together; the audio event and mix model is not re-derived here and contributes no evidence for haptic semantics

Ranks haptics twelfth and records that every one of the three benchmark product shapes needs it from the first minute; this is the motivating gap the queue candidate answers, not evidence for the common kernel

States that a package manifest or one successful profile does not prove other Unity, XRI, OpenXR runtime, or device tuples; this family's Unity-adapter admitted role for every OpenXR extension source is bounded by that policy rather than by the extension's own text

source_gate_non_claims: No source grants package maturity, release, certification, platform review outcome, or device authority

The first implementation is a HapticEventId, closed-kind, profile, and immutable-state substrate with a binding table and a thin Unity adapter; it is not a haptic clip authoring tool, not a waveform editor, and admits no claim that any named controller or headset supports amplitude-envelope or PCM haptics

The family guarantees the plumbing only: that an accepted play, stop, stop-all, or set-profile intent reached the injectable output sink with the exact target, amplitude, duration, and frequency it computed; whether a controller vibrated, and how it felt, is a human judgement recorded in a Device Lab receipt
Felt intensity, comfort, fatigue, and whether a pattern reads as intended are Device Lab receipts, never package claims, and no test in this family's gates claims a controller vibrated

Automated or device evidence recorded for one controller, headset, or OpenXR runtime tuple never transfers to another controller, headset, or runtime, and envelope or PCM support proven on one device is never assumed on another
